label: CKD N06A
title: Duloxetine supplied below a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min
statement: In an outpatient aged 18 or older with established chronic kidney disease, review any oral duloxetine supply when the Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance applicable at supply is below 30 mL/min.

source.document: A systematically collated library of prescribing safety indicators for people with chronic kidney disease, Additional file 2 (Appendix 3)
source.citation: Smith F, Hayward S, Hole B, Kimpton G, Sluman C, Whiting P, Caskey F. BMC Nephrology. 2020;21:493.

plain_summary: Review oral duloxetine in an adult outpatient with established CKD when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min. Australian product information for Cymbalta and Duloxetine-WGR specifies 30 mg once daily at this clearance. Check the product and prescribed dose during review.

medicine_groups.name: Duloxetine
medicine_groups.note: Any oral duloxetine product or brand counts at any strength. A missing daily dose does not prevent a renal review.

needs_facts.meets: Use the dated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance in mL/min applicable at supply. Below 30 mL/min meets at any oral dose. A value of 30 mL/min or higher excludes. An undated result of uncertain timing, an indexed eGFR or an unknown answer leaves clearance unresolved.
The adult has established chronic kidney disease in outpatient care.

rule_for_models: For an outpatient aged 18 or older with established CKD at supply, report a renal medicine review for any oral duloxetine dose if the applicable dated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min. Cite the supply, CKD and clearance. This finding does not establish an overdose or contraindication. Give no finding at 30 mL/min or higher or if any eligibility condition fails. Otherwise, if age, CKD or outpatient status at supply, or the dated clearance is unknown, cite the supply and available evidence, report a possible finding and ask for the missing detail. Name "Chronic kidney disease" only when CKD remains unresolved and its answer could change the finding. An undated counter entry alone cannot establish when CKD began or when clearance was measured. Accept a dated result labelled Creatinine clearance if its method and unit match.
cannot_be_seen: Ask whether the patient has chronic kidney disease and check for a dated Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance relevant to the supply. An eGFR or a serum creatinine value alone does not provide that result. Supply does not establish the dose taken.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm creatinine clearance and review the dose against the information for the duloxetine product supplied?
